In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta an independent evaluation relays that forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, and that the zones around mangrove roots protected from the violence of the sea created breeding grounds for fish and shellfish, with sea crabs and shellfish re-appearing in some places and increasing in others [ev_frmg_vnppar_3, ev_frmg_vnppar_4].
conditionality: The same meta-analysis found no major difference in crab or fish production and diversity between restored mangroves and unvegetated tidal flats, and its metric merges production with diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_2], so the gain depends on the comparison: it holds against degraded mangrove, not against the open tidal flat. Over longer periods, successful rehabilitation can raise soil carbon by 83 to 96 Mg C/ha [ev_soil_organic_carbon_ellison20_4]. Successful rehabilitation can raise soil carbon by 83 to 96 Mg C/ha over longer periods [ev_soil_organic_carbon_ellison20_4], and existing mangrove soils that build up as sea level rises keep adding about 1.3–2.0 Mg C per hectare each year [ev_carbon_sequestration_sanderman18_4]. Clearing mangroves releases this store: converting mangrove to shrimp ponds lost 90% of soil carbon in the top 3 m in one study [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sanderman18_2], and 54% of below-ground carbon on average after conversion to ponds and pasture in another [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sanderman18_3].

effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts reduce coastal flooding by breaking waves and, more weakly, lowering surge water as it passes through the forest [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3]. Existing mangroves cut wave heights by 31% in a meta-analysis of field measurements [ev_frmg_nara16_1], and measured surge peaks fall by 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of mangrove [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1]. A global model finds that losing current mangroves would flood 28% more people each year [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1], and a Philippine model gives 24% more [ev_flood_hazard_wbphl17_1]. In India and Bangladesh, villages sheltered by existing mangrove forest took less salt water and flood water after super cyclones [ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7, ev_flood_hazard_akber18_7]. The avoided damage has been put in money terms: in Orissa mangroves protected houses worth USD 1218 per hectare of forest in a single cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and mangroves in front of sea dykes cut repair costs by 20–30% [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10]. Of restoration projects reviewed, 50% report better storm protection [ev_frmg_nara16_5].

The village surveys are small and their authors call them only indicative [ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7, ev_flood_hazard_akber18_7], and the money values are avoided damage to society, not income to the households working the coast [ev_economic_return_das11_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_1]. effect_mechanism: Mangrove restoration reaches household incomes mainly through fish, crabs and shellfish. In northern Viet Nam mangroves raised per-hectare yields of shellfish and oysters by 209-789 per cent, adding income for coastal communities [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. In a rehabilitated basin in Java a new finfish fishery earns fishers about 1.05 USD per hour [ev_household_income_debrot22_2], and a Philippine survey suggests replanted mangroves add USD 564–2316/ha/y to local incomes [ev_household_income_debrot22_3]. Appraisals of the planting itself are mostly positive: a global meta-analysis finds benefits outweigh costs [ev_economic_return_su21_1], commune benefit-cost ratios in Viet Nam range from 3.06 to 68.92 [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1], and Mexican pilot sites had positive net present values [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. A Senegal model assumes women's income from oyster gathering rises by 10% [ev_household_income_iisd26_4].
